Challenge C088-CH2: Membranes in dairy plants foul quickly and need cleaning every week.
Detail: At two dairy plants we service — one near Temerin, one outside

content.text: {"expertise":[{"text":"Membrane fouling can be characterised using blocking models and rheological analysis to distinguish between cake formation, intermediate blocking, and complete blocking mechanisms depending on feed composition and operating pressure.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-02395","field":"abstract","quote":"Hermia's blocking models (complete, intermediate, standard blocking and cake filtration) were fitted to flux–time data."}]},{"text":"Activated sludge systems can be acclimated to treat complex organic substrates, with respirometric measurement and biomass morphology assessment used to track adaptation over weeks to months and predict steady-state biodegradation performance.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-02390","field":"abstract","quote":"Respirometric measurements showed that oxygen uptake rate stabilised within 21 days at 10% dye effluent fraction"}]},{"text":"Coagulation-flocculation pretreatment can remove specific organic compounds more or less effectively depending on molecular structure and charge properties, with jar testing and sludge characterisation providing design parameters for polishing steps.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-02387","field":"abstract","quote":"dye charge density and molecular weight significantly influence coagulation efficiency"}]}],"fit":"partial","fitReason":"The researcher has expertise in activated sludge acclimation, respirometric analysis, and membrane fouling mechanics [SYN-PUB-02390, SYN-PUB-02395], but prior work focuses on textile and fermentation streams rather than dairy wastewater; membrane material selection and fat-protein interaction chemistry are not addressed in the record."}
